core.title: Name every feature slug verb-object
core.given: A plan contains feature plan artifacts with feature URNs (new, renamed or unchanged)
core.when: The planner names a feature slug (the name segment of the feature URN) or the plan reaches the CONFIRM phase
core.then: Every feature slug is verb-object: kebab-case, at least two tokens, the leading token a verb from the verb-selection lexicon, and no connective tokens.
prefer: A leading verb taken from the plan's verb-selection lexicon, followed by the object it acts on
Slugs that read as one verb plus its object, naming the single behaviour the feature delivers
When a slug must be a brand or proper noun, list it explicitly in the naming-exception list
avoid: Connective slugs that chain two behaviours or route to a target — split into separate features or rename to one verb-object
Single-token slugs, or a first token outside the verb-selection lexicon
Implicit brand/proper-noun exceptions — an unlisted exception is a violation
unless: The slug is a brand or proper noun explicitly listed in the naming-exception list
core.why: A verb-object slug names the single behaviour a feature delivers, keeping features atomic and names consistent; connectives signal bundled behaviours.
evidence: The CONFIRM-phase naming check passes over every feature slug in the plan
On failure the check reports the offending feature URN and the reason
verification: Subject is the feature plan artifact: at the CONFIRM phase a naming check parses the name segment of the feature URN (per the profile's feature URN shape) for every feature in the plan — not only changed ones — and requires kebab-case, at least two tokens, a leading token from the verb-selection lexicon, and no connective tokens (e.g. and, to)
The check exempts only slugs explicitly listed in the naming-exception list; an unlisted brand/proper-noun slug is a violation
Enforcement is confirm-blocking: a failure blocks the CONFIRM phase, and the finding reports the offending feature URN and the reason
The check is exercised against known-good verb-object slugs and known-bad connective or single-token slugs (concrete fixtures live in the reference realization)
Out of scope: naming of wagons, WMBTs or acceptances — the check covers feature slugs only

fires: The planner adds a feature artifact with a feature URN
The planner renames an existing feature slug
CONFIRM validation runs over a plan containing features, including unchanged slugs whose feature body alone was edited
doesNotFire: The plan contains no feature URNs (only wagons, WMBTs or acceptances)
Naming a wagon, WMBT or acceptance rather than a feature slug

profileRequirements.meaning: URN shape of a feature plan artifact; the core identifies the slug as the URN's name segment (the 3rd segment in the Bun shape)
Where the stack declares the verb-selection lexicon: the allowed leading verbs for verb-object names
Where naming-rule exceptions such as brand/proper-noun slugs must be explicitly listed; an unlisted exception is a violation

neutralityNotes: The convention is essentially stack-neutral already: it constrains plan-artifact naming, not code. 'kebab-case' is kept in the core because it is part of the naming pattern being imposed, not a stack mechanism; a stack whose feature URN slugs were shaped differently would still be held to kebab-case by this core, which matches the Bun obligation exactly. 'CONFIRM' and 'confirm-blocking' are ATDD harness/process concepts and stay in the core. Two profile keys had to be proposed because the closed vocabulary has no key for a naming verb lexicon or a naming-exception allow-list; until they are approved, each realization supplies these locations from its own convention bundle. Concrete example and fixture slugs live only in the reference realization (bun.json).
